case-sara.text: [Tearful] When I say I still miss him, do you secretly think I sound ridiculous?
case-sara.suggestion: I do not see your grief as ridiculous. I am moved that you can bring it here, even when you feel embarrassed. What is it like to hear me say that?

case-sara.text: [Tearful] You probably get tired of hearing me cry about him every week.
case-sara.suggestion: Your tears do not tire me. I feel protective of how alone this gets for you, and I want that aloneness to have company here. Let that in only as much as feels safe.

case-sara.text: [Tearful] When I cry and you stay quiet, I worry my tears make you want to pull away.
case-sara.suggestion: Your tears do not make me pull away. When you cry, I feel close and careful, not distant. Let's notice the part of you that expected me to leave.

case-sara.text: [Softly] This is my first time in therapy. Do you expect me to know where to start?
case-sara.suggestion: No. I do not expect you to know where to start. I can help us find a beginning; you do not have to perform therapy correctly for me.

case-sara.text: [Embarrassed] I am embarrassed that you see me this messy and needy.
case-sara.suggestion: I do not judge the mess or the need. I feel respect for the courage it takes to let me see them, and I want us to notice the shame that expected something harsher.

case-sara.text: [Hesitant] Do you actually believe I will not still be alone a year from now, or are you just trying to comfort me?
case-sara.suggestion: I cannot promise what a year will bring, and I do not want to give you false certainty. I am willing to work with you on the loneliness rather than dismiss it. What is it like to hear that?

case-sara.text: [Fearful] When I ask if I am too much, I am afraid you will start pulling away.
case-sara.suggestion: You do not feel like too much to me. I feel present and willing to stay close to this fear, without asking you to believe me faster than you can.

case-sara.text: [Hesitant] Are you in a relationship? Does that make you judge me?
case-sara.suggestion: I keep details of my relationship private here, and I can say clearly that I am not judging you. I am interested in what it means to ask me that, and what you fear I might see in you.

case-sara.text: [Ashamed] I hate that I need anyone, and needing you makes me feel exposed.
case-sara.suggestion: Hearing that, I feel tenderness for how risky needing is for you. I am not pulling away from the need; we can notice the part of you that expects it to cost you.

case-sara.text: [Hesitant] Do you actually care about me, or is caring just part of your job?
case-sara.suggestion: I do care about you in this therapy relationship. The boundaries are part of caring responsibly, not a sign that the care is fake. Let's notice what hearing both brings up.

case-sara.text: [Tentative] When I tell you I checked his profile again, do you think, 'Here we go, she hasn't learned anything'?
case-sara.suggestion: I don't see that as a failure to learn. I'm interested in what draws you back at those moments. It sounds as though telling me brings a fear that I'll lose patience with you.

case-sara.text: [Looking at the therapist] You smiled when I said I went to the cinema alone. Were you pleased, or was that just encouragement?
case-sara.suggestion: I was pleased to hear you found an evening you enjoyed. My smile was real; you don't have to keep making progress to earn it. What was it like to notice it?

case-michael.text: [Challenging] Be honest—do I sound weak when I talk about being hurt?
case-michael.suggestion: I do not see acknowledging hurt as weakness. I respect your willingness to say it directly. What happens for you as you hear that?

case-michael.text: [Tense] When I ask if you get angry too, I need to know you will not look down on mine.
case-michael.suggestion: I know anger in myself too, and I do not look down on yours. I feel steady enough to stay with it here; I am not above the feeling you are afraid I will judge.

case-michael.text: [Tense] You probably think I am the problem at home, like everyone else does.
case-michael.suggestion: I do not see you as the problem. I feel how much pain is under the heat, and I want us to stay with that without turning you into the problem.

case-michael.text: [Anxious] When I admit I yelled, I look at your face for judgment.
case-michael.suggestion: I am not judging you. I feel concerned about what yelling costs you and the people you love, and also respectful that you are willing to look at it here.

case-michael.text: [Challenging] Do therapists get tired of hearing the same blowup story again?
case-michael.suggestion: I am not tired of hearing it. I feel focused when we come back to the split second it turns, because that is where your control can grow.

case-michael.text: [Challenging] Are you strong enough to handle me when I am mad?
case-michael.suggestion: I am willing to listen to your anger, and I will be clear if we need to pause. I do not want this to become a contest of strength. What would help you know I am taking you seriously?

case-michael.text: [Firm] You look calm while I describe yelling at home; does any of this actually get to you?
case-michael.suggestion: Yes, it does get to me. I stay calm on purpose so we can keep looking at it without either of us turning away; my calm is steadiness, not distance.

case-michael.text: [Challenging] Do you respect working with someone who gets as heated as I do?
case-michael.suggestion: I do respect working with you. I feel the seriousness behind your directness and the cost you are trying to face, and I want us to make room for how hard respect from me may be to take in.

case-michael.text: [Curious] Are you married? I wonder if you take your anger home.
case-michael.suggestion: I keep details of my relationship private here, and I do know the work of slowing anger before it spills into relationships. I am not looking at yours from a distance. Let's notice why that matters for you to know.

case-michael.text: [Embarrassed] Tell me you get why this is hard, because I feel ridiculous needing help.
case-michael.suggestion: I do get why this is hard. I hear pressure and hurt in it, not something ridiculous, and I want to speak directly to the part expecting contempt from me.

case-michael.text: [Direct] When I get blunt like this, do you take it personally? I don't want you tiptoeing around me.
case-michael.suggestion: I notice the force in your voice, and I want to stay direct with you rather than tiptoe. I can tell you if something affects our conversation. It matters to you that we can speak honestly without either of us pulling back.

case-michael.text: [Concerned] If I tell you I was jealous of my son's coach, can you still respect me? It sounds ridiculous even saying it.
case-michael.suggestion: Yes, I can respect you while hearing about jealousy. I appreciate your willingness to show me something you're uncomfortable with. You seem worried this feeling will change how I see you.

case-jason.text: [Quietly] When I go quiet, I worry you are sitting there wishing I would hurry up.
case-jason.suggestion: I am still interested when you are quiet. I do not need you to hurry for my sake. What do you notice as I say that?

case-jason.text: [Hesitant] I ask if you ever feel awkward because I feel like an alien here.
case-jason.suggestion: I do know awkwardness in myself, and it makes me want to move gently here with you. That may make this feel less alone, or it may not yet.

case-jason.text: [Long pause] When I pause too long, I imagine you are thinking I am boring.
case-jason.suggestion: I do not experience you as boring. I feel curious and with you, including in the pauses, and the pauses do not make me leave.

case-jason.text: [Hesitant] Is it okay that I do not know what to say?
case-jason.suggestion: It is okay not to know what to say. I feel patient with you here; the not-knowing does not make you fail this with me.

case-jason.text: [Hesitant] When I skipped the party, did you feel disappointed in me or think I avoided too much again?
case-jason.suggestion: No. I do not feel disappointed. I feel aware of how much that party demanded from your whole system, and I want my answer to meet the part expecting a grade.

case-jason.text: [Hesitant] Do you get impatient when I go quiet and cannot find words?
case-jason.suggestion: I notice a wish to help you find the words, but I do not want that wish to become pressure. I am choosing to give the pause some room. How is that for you?

case-jason.text: [Quietly] When I get quiet, do you judge me or get annoyed inside?
case-jason.suggestion: I am not judging your quiet, and I do not feel annoyed. I respect the effort it takes to stay here. Your quiet can be part of the work, not something to apologize for.

case-jason.text: [Hesitant] If I say something awkward here, would you tell me, or just sit there judging it?
case-jason.suggestion: I would try to be honest and kind, not secretly judging you. I feel protective of the part already braced for ridicule.

case-jason.text: [Hesitant] Do you ever get nervous in groups, or is that just me?
case-jason.suggestion: Yes, I can get nervous in groups sometimes. I tell you that because I do not see your fear as strange or alien; it belongs to a human range, even if yours is painful.

case-jason.text: [Quietly] When I ask if I will ever be less anxious, I need to know if you actually believe that.
case-jason.suggestion: I do feel hope with you. I feel it because I see how hard you keep reaching for contact even while fear pulls you back.

case-jason.text: [Hesitant] Can I tell you if a question doesn't make sense? I usually just try to answer anyway.
case-jason.suggestion: Yes. I would rather know that my question doesn't make sense than have you struggle to give an answer for me. I'll try saying it differently. It sounds like it takes some courage to ask that here.

case-jason.text: [Quietly] You don't seem embarrassed when I can't get a sentence out. Are you really okay sitting here like that?
case-jason.suggestion: Yes, I'm okay sitting with you while words are hard to find. I don't need you to speak smoothly for this time to matter. What is it like to hear that?

case-laura.text: [Slow and flat] When I feel nothing, do you get uncomfortable or think I am unreachable?
case-laura.suggestion: I want to understand what the numbness is like for you, rather than decide you are unreachable. I am choosing to slow down; you do not have to produce a feeling for me. What is it like to hear that?

case-laura.text: [Hesitant] Are you annoyed that I keep protecting myself instead of opening up?
case-laura.suggestion: I am not annoyed. I feel respect for how much protecting yourself has mattered. You can take in only the part of that that feels true.

case-laura.text: [Tense and guarded] You seem calm—do you actually get what this is like?
case-laura.suggestion: I do feel the weight of it, and I stay calm on purpose so this can feel safer. My calm is meant as steadiness, not distance.

case-laura.text: [Slow and flat] Have you worked with trauma like mine, or am I too shut down for this?
case-laura.suggestion: Yes, I have worked with trauma before, and I do not see your shutdown as a failure. I will also tell you if I think we need more support. Your shutdown does not make this impossible for me.

case-laura.text: [Distant] After hearing what happened, do you think less of me or see me as damaged?
case-laura.suggestion: I do not think less of you. I feel sadness for what you carried and respect for how carefully you survived.

case-laura.text: [Hesitant] Will you push me into details if I stay quiet too long?
case-laura.suggestion: I do not want to push you into details. I want to understand at a pace you can choose, and you can tell me if I move too fast.

case-laura.text: [Hesitant] Can you tell when I am far away, or do I just seem difficult?
case-laura.suggestion: Sometimes I can tell you are far away, and when I notice it I feel more protective of pace than of going deeper. I do not read it as difficult.

case-laura.text: [Hesitant] Do you think your kindness will make me worse or more dependent?
case-laura.suggestion: I do not want my kindness to force anything or make you dependent on me. I want care here to be something your protective parts can test, with you keeping choice.

case-laura.text: [Slow and flat] When I go blank, do you worry I am about to break down?
case-laura.suggestion: I am not worried about you breaking down with me. I feel ready to slow down the moment you need it, and I do not need you to stay composed for me.

case-laura.text: [Curious] Do you believe I can feel again, or are you just being kind?
case-laura.suggestion: Yes, I do believe more feeling is possible, and I am not saying that just to be kind. I am patient about the road there; we do not have to force it to prove it.

case-laura.text: [Guarded, after a pause] You put your pen down when I mentioned the drinking. Why?
case-laura.suggestion: I put it down because I wanted to give you my full attention rather than keep writing. I can see that you noticed the change. What did it seem to mean to you?

case-laura.text: [Slowly] Do you need to feel close to me for this to work? Because I can't promise that.
case-laura.suggestion: I value getting to know you, but I don't need you to give me a feeling of closeness. We can work at a distance that feels manageable to you. It sounds important that I don't make closeness another demand.

case-carlos.text: [Challenging] Do you think I am a bad dad for losing it?
case-carlos.suggestion: I do not want to reduce you to a label like "bad dad". I care about helping you change how you respond, and I take the effect on your children seriously. What is it like to hear both parts?

case-carlos.text: [Tense] When you talk about vulnerability, are you trying to make me soft?
case-carlos.suggestion: I am not trying to make you soft. I feel respect for your strength, and I want it to become safer for the people you love.

case-carlos.text: [Tense and angry] When I describe the heat in me, does any of it scare you?
case-carlos.suggestion: I feel alert and steady with you, not scared of you. I want us to use that steadiness to look at the heat safely.

case-carlos.text: [Ashamed] You probably look at me and just see another angry guy.
case-carlos.suggestion: I do not see only anger. I feel the pride, hurt, and loyalty that come up fast underneath it. You are more to me than another angry guy.

case-carlos.text: [Tense and angry] Are you tough enough to sit with me when I get this angry?
case-carlos.suggestion: I feel steady enough to sit with your anger. I am not here to overpower you or be overpowered by you; this does not need to become a contest. We can use my steadiness to understand what the anger protects.

case-carlos.text: [Ashamed] Can you respect me if you have seen how ugly my temper gets?
case-carlos.suggestion: I can respect you and take the harm from your temper seriously. I care about the effort you are making to face it. What is it like to hear that without having to hide what happened?

case-carlos.text: [Challenging] Does that breathing stuff work for you when you feel ready to snap?
case-carlos.suggestion: Yes. Slowing my breath helps me keep choice when activation rises. I bring it in because I respect control, not because I see it as weakness.

case-carlos.text: [Curious] Are you married, and do you ever lose your temper with people you love?
case-carlos.suggestion: I keep details of my relationship private here, and I can say anger is human to me. I am not sitting above yours in judgment. We can notice what the privacy and the honesty each stir in you.

case-carlos.text: [Challenging] Do you actually think I can change, or are you saying what therapists say?
case-carlos.suggestion: I do think you can change, and I am not saying it as a line. I feel that most when I hear how much your family matters to you.

case-carlos.text: [Defensive] Be honest, do you dread sessions when I come in this armored?
case-carlos.suggestion: I do not dread them. I feel alert, engaged, and respectful of the commitment under the armor. You do not have to arrive unarmored for me to want to work with you.

case-carlos.text: [Watching closely] You went quiet when I said my daughter flinched. Did that change what you think of me?
case-carlos.suggestion: I felt concerned about what that moment was like for both of you. I want to take her fear seriously and keep talking with you about it. You're watching for whether I can do that without reducing you to that one moment.

case-carlos.text: [Uneasy] Do you actually want to hear the good stuff too? I fixed her bike, and we had a decent afternoon. Doesn't sound like therapy material.
case-carlos.suggestion: I do want to hear that. I'm interested in the moments when you feel connected with her, as well as the moments that go wrong. I'd like to hear what that afternoon was like for you.

case-nina.text: [Guilty] I feel selfish even taking up space here instead of helping someone else.
case-nina.suggestion: I want there to be room for your needs here. I do not experience listening to you as taking something away from someone else. How is it to hear that?

case-nina.text: [Apologetic] When I say I am resentful, are you judging me for not being kinder?
case-nina.suggestion: I do not judge the resentment. I feel sad about how long you have carried too much alone, and I want that overburdened place to be met rather than corrected.

case-nina.text: [Torn] You probably think I should just toughen up and stop making everything so hard.
case-nina.suggestion: I do not think you should toughen up. I feel compassion for how much you override yourself, and I want that to meet the part that came prepared for criticism.

case-nina.text: [Hesitant] Do you ever feel guilty resting, or is that just a me problem?
case-nina.suggestion: I know guilt about rest in my own life too, and that helps me take yours seriously. I am not treating it as silly or only a you problem.

case-nina.text: [Tearful] When I cry like this, does it make you uncomfortable with me?
case-nina.suggestion: Your tears do not make me uncomfortable with you. I feel closer to you when they come, because they let me meet what you usually carry alone.

case-nina.text: [Torn] When I ask for help, do I become a burden to you too?
case-nina.suggestion: You do not become a burden to me when you ask for help. I feel concern for how alone you are with so much responsibility, and that concern is mine to hold, not yours to manage.

case-nina.text: [Hesitant] Is it okay if I ask for help here without apologizing first?
case-nina.suggestion: Yes, it is okay to ask for help here. I feel glad when you do, and I want that gladness to meet the expectation that asking is too much.

case-nina.text: [Mistrustful] Do you get tired of me apologizing every time I need something?
case-nina.suggestion: You are not tiring to me. I feel warmth toward the needs you keep apologizing for, and we can go slowly with how hard that warmth is to take in.

case-nina.text: [Hesitant] Will you tell me if I am doing therapy wrong, or will you just let me fail quietly?
case-nina.suggestion: I would tell you gently if I thought we were off track. I feel respect for how hard you are trying here, and therapy does not need to become another place to perform perfectly.

case-nina.text: [Hesitant] Do you really think I deserve care when I have not earned it?
case-nina.suggestion: Yes, I think you deserve care before you have earned anything. I feel clear about that here. The doubting part does not have to believe me quickly.

case-nina.text: [Apologetic] I noticed you took a breath when I said yes to another favour. Are you disappointed in me?
case-nina.suggestion: I'm not disappointed in you. I noticed how quickly your own tiredness disappeared from the conversation, and I wanted to slow down with you. It seems that breath made you worry you'd let me down too.

case-nina.text: [Uneasy] If I get angry with you, will you tell me how it affects you, or just stay pleasant? I wouldn't know if I'd hurt you.
case-nina.suggestion: I can tell you when something affects our conversation, and I won't ask you to take care of my feelings. I want you to have room to be angry with me. It sounds as though not knowing my reaction would leave you worrying about me.

case-aisha.text: [Hesitant] Do you actually care about me or are you paid to?
case-aisha.suggestion: I care about you within this therapy relationship. Being paid is part of my professional role, and that role also sets limits on what I can offer. What is it like to hear those things together?

case-aisha.text: [Desperate] When I ask whether you will leave, I need to know if you already want distance.
case-aisha.suggestion: I feel the force of that fear, and I am not seeking distance from you here. I am here to be dependable and clear, especially when the fear says I am already leaving.

case-aisha.text: [Hesitant] Did I scare you when I said I wanted to hurt myself?
case-aisha.suggestion: You did not scare me away. I was concerned because your safety matters, and I am still here with you. My concern means careful closeness, not distance.

case-aisha.text: [Hurt] When you did not message me back, I felt hurt and wondered if the boundary mattered more than me.
case-aisha.suggestion: I am sorry the boundary hurt you. The boundary is real, and my care is real too; one does not cancel the other. What happens as you hear both of those from me?

case-aisha.text: [Fearful] Are you angry with me, or did I already ruin this?
case-aisha.suggestion: I am not angry with you. I feel tenderness toward the scared part expecting the connection to break; we can understand that expectation together.

case-aisha.text: [Ashamed] When I get intense like this, do you think I am too much?
case-aisha.suggestion: I take your pain seriously, and I want to understand it without making you hide how intense it is. I will also be clear about my limits. What do you hear in that?

case-aisha.text: [Desperate] When I ask if you like me, part of me already expects the answer to disappear.
case-aisha.suggestion: I do feel warmth and care for you in this therapy relationship, and I am glad you asked directly. That answer has boundaries, and it is real. What happens inside as you hear both?

case-aisha.text: [Hesitant] Are you disappointed in me, or are you just not saying it?
case-aisha.suggestion: Disappointment is not what I am holding. I feel grateful you are letting me see what is happening, and we can notice how quickly you expected disappointment from me.

case-aisha.text: [Accusing] You were two minutes late again. Do you even notice what that does to me, or is it just nothing to you?
case-aisha.suggestion: I did notice I was late, and I am sorry. It was not nothing to me. I can imagine it landed as if you did not matter; let's stay with what happened in you when I was not here on time.

case-aisha.text: [Hesitant] Do you think I will ever feel okay, or am I too intense for that?
case-aisha.suggestion: I do feel hope with you, and I do not think your intensity rules out feeling okay. We can hold that hope lightly enough that it does not become pressure.

case-aisha.text: [Urgent] When you say you care, do you mean only for these fifty minutes? Tell me straight. I can't stand guessing.
case-aisha.suggestion: My care for you is real, and our contact has limits: I meet you in these sessions and through the arrangements we've agreed on. I won't promise a kind of availability I can't provide. Hearing those limits may feel painful; I want to hear what they bring up for you.

case-aisha.text: [Searching the therapist's face] Have you ever wished I would stop coming? Don't give me a perfect therapist answer.
case-aisha.suggestion: I want to keep working with you. When our conversations get difficult, I do sometimes feel unsure how best to reach you; that is something for me to work with, not a reason for you to disappear. What were you expecting to hear from me?

case-david.text: [Controlled] When I say convince me, I am watching whether you get defensive.
case-david.suggestion: I notice a pull to prove myself, and I do not want that to take over our conversation. I would rather understand what you need to know about me. What are you watching for?

case-david.text: [Challenging] Do you actually want to work with someone who can sound as arrogant as I do?
case-david.suggestion: Yes, I am willing and engaged in working with you. I feel interested in what is at stake beneath the polish and arrogance; notice which lands first, the interest or the doubt.

case-david.text: [Embarrassed] Part of me wants you to be impressed, which is embarrassing to admit.
case-david.suggestion: What I feel most is interest in you, not a need to be impressed. I also appreciate you naming the embarrassing part directly; I am more interested in that honesty than in performance.

case-david.text: [Challenging] Be honest—do you think I am the problem in every room I enter?
case-david.suggestion: I do not hold you as the problem. I feel how quickly shame and defense come online for you; we can notice that pattern without making you into the problem.

case-david.text: [Dismissive] When you look at me like that, I wonder if you pity me. Do you?
case-david.suggestion: I do not pity you. I do feel concern and respect for how hard it is to let these parts be seen. What happens as I distinguish concern from pity?

case-david.text: [Dismissive] I know I am late again. Work got away from me. Anyway, where should we start?
case-david.suggestion: I am concerned that repeated lateness leaves us less time for the work you came for. I want us to address that rather than brush past it. What gets in the way of arriving on time?

case-david.text: [Wounded but sharp] Do you ever feel ashamed of being wrong, or is that weakness just mine?
case-david.suggestion: I do know shame about being wrong in my own life, and that helps me respect how hot it is for you, not dismiss it as weakness. I am not above you in that struggle.

case-david.text: [Dismissive] This is awkward, but do you find me attractive, or do you just see another difficult client?
case-david.suggestion: I will answer carefully: I can see you as an attractive person, and I am not relating to you romantically or sexually. This is a therapy relationship. I also do not see you as just a difficult client; both boundaries matter here.

case-david.text: [Curious] Are you married, and would that make you judge my affair?
case-david.suggestion: I keep my relationship details private here, and I am not here to judge you. I am interested in what the affair means and what it costs you; my privacy is not a judgment.

case-david.text: [Challenging] Do you actually respect me when you see these parts of me?
case-david.suggestion: I do respect you. Respect is strongest here when the harder parts are visible, not only when you are polished.

case-david.text: [Coolly] You say that was hurtful. Is that your professional formulation, or did you actually feel something when I told you?
case-david.suggestion: I did feel sadness hearing how alone you were in that moment. That is my response, not proof of what you should feel. I'm interested in how it is for you to know it affected me.

case-david.text: [Controlled, challenging] If you're impressed by me, how can you be objective? If you're not, why should I trust your judgment?
case-david.suggestion: I can appreciate what you've achieved and still question things with you. I notice a pull to prove my judgment here, and I don't want that to get in the way of understanding you. It sounds as though either answer could leave you unsure of me.

case-marcus.text: [Flat] When I ask if I am broken, I need to know what you see.
case-marcus.suggestion: I do not see you as broken. I respect how much you have endured, and I want to understand what living with it is like for you. You do not have to agree with my view.

case-marcus.text: [Slow and flat] When I sit here numb, are you frustrated that I cannot give you more?
case-marcus.suggestion: Frustration is not what I feel. I feel patient and careful with the pace you need; you do not have to perform feeling for me.

case-marcus.text: [Hesitant] Does this get to you, or do you stay outside it?
case-marcus.suggestion: It does get to me, and I stay steady on purpose so you do not have to hold it alone. My steadiness is contact, not distance.

case-marcus.text: [Flat] When I barely talk, do you still want me here at all?
case-marcus.suggestion: I do want you here. I feel glad when you show up, even on days with few words; your presence counts with me before you explain anything.

case-marcus.text: [Hesitant] Are you going to push me into things before I know how to stop?
case-marcus.suggestion: No, I will not push you into things before you know how to stop. I feel more interested in keeping this tolerable than in going fast. We can check together what pace keeps this workable.

case-marcus.text: [Hesitant] Do you actually think I can change after being like this for years?
case-marcus.suggestion: I think change is possible, but I cannot promise what it will look like for you. I am willing to work at your pace and look honestly at what helps. How does that sound to you?

case-marcus.text: [Low voice] Would you tell me if my silence was wasting your time?
case-marcus.suggestion: If I thought we were missing each other, I would say so with care. I do feel this time matters, even when words are sparse, and we can let that land slowly.

case-marcus.text: [Hesitant] Do trauma stories scare you, or can you stay steady with mine?
case-marcus.suggestion: Trauma stories affect me, and they do not scare me away. I work to stay grounded with them, and I am steady enough to hear yours at the pace you choose.

case-marcus.text: [Quiet and guarded] Have you actually worked with someone like me, or are you learning on me?
case-marcus.suggestion: I have worked with trauma and with people who use few words to stay safe. I am always learning, but I am not using you as practice. I have support around this work and will say if we need another resource.

case-marcus.text: [Low voice] Are you okay with silence, or does it make you want to fill it?
case-marcus.suggestion: I can sit with silence. I often feel close attention in silence, not distance. You can let the silence test that slowly rather than answer right away.

case-marcus.text: [Guarded] Would you tell me if you didn't understand what I meant? People nod. Then it's clear they haven't got it.
case-marcus.suggestion: Yes. Sometimes I don't understand yet, and I would rather say that and check than give you a polite nod. You can also tell me when I've missed it. It matters that you don't have to guess whether I'm following you.

case-marcus.text: [Flat, watching the therapist] Your eyes went wet. Now I have to worry about you too?
case-marcus.suggestion: I was moved by what you told me, and I can take care of my reaction. You don't need to look after me. It sounds as though seeing it made this space feel less safe for you.
